summary: Chelan County summit cabin: 1923 per register and Wikipedia (Willhite says 1926), decommissioned 1949, gone by 1955; now a National Park Service radio repeater.

facts.status_note: The cabin is gone; the summit now has a National Park Service radio repeater (Wikipedia)

staffing.status: Paul Heaton named as the lookout in the 1926 construction account

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (per the register, for the years the cabin stood)

access.note: Summit trail starts near High Bridge Guard Station on the Stehekin Valley Road; these sources describe no closure or permit, and the final stretch is exposed scrambling

visit.trail_note: No lookout remains to climb. The 7.7-mile McGregor Mountain Trail gains 6,400 feet; the last 1,100 feet is exposed scrambling (Wikipedia)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register, Firelookout.com, Wikipedia and WTA put the cabin at 1923; Willhite Web dates construction to 1926. The built event uses 1923 and the story reports both.
Register says removed in 1955, Firelookout.com says destroyed, and Willhite Web says the Forest Service burned it. All three are reported; the event is marked burned, per Willhite Web's account.

notes_for_editor: Two coordinate sets are in the brief. The register point (48.40322, -120.76001) is about 3 km from the Wikipedia summit coordinates (48.408178, -120.798239), which match the other set; the record keeps the register point, and an editor should confirm which marks the lookout. Built date (1923 vs 1926) and end (removed vs destroyed vs burned) disagree across sources; both are reported. Access 'public' is inferred from trail descriptions with no closure mentioned; confirm before publishing. Staffing is one name from the 1926 account.
